meaning: I is a word you use to talk about yourself. It is the subject pronoun for the speaker. For example, 'I am happy' means the person speaking feels happy.
You is a word used to talk to the person or people you are speaking with. It does not matter if it is one person or many. For example, 'You are my friend' means the listener is a friend.
He is used to talk about a boy or a man. Instead of repeating the name, we use 'he'. For example, 'This is Tom. He is my brother.'
She is used to talk about a girl or a woman. It replaces the name to avoid repetition. For example, 'This is Anna. She is kind.'
We means the speaker together with other people. It shows more than one person including yourself. For example, 'We are going to school' means you and others are going.
They is used to talk about more than one person, animal, or thing. For example, 'They are my friends' means several people are friends. It avoids repeating names.
Have means to own, hold, or experience something. For example, 'I have a car' means the car belongs to you. It can also mean to do activities, like 'have lunch'.
Come means to move closer to the speaker or a place. For example, 'Please come here' means move to where I am. It often shows movement toward someone.
Want means to wish for something or feel a need. For example, 'I want pizza' means you feel like eating pizza. It shows desire or preference.
Eat means to take food into your mouth and chew or swallow it. For example, 'I eat rice every day.' Eating gives your body energy to live and grow.
Drink means to take liquid into your mouth and swallow it. For example, 'I drink water when I am thirsty.' It is necessary to stay healthy and alive.
Get means to receive, obtain, or take something. For example, 'I get a gift' means you receive it. It can also mean to become, like 'get tired'.
A woman is an adult female human. Women are often daughters, sisters, mothers, or workers in society. For example, 'The woman is a teacher.'
A friend is a person you like and spend time with. Friends support and help each other. For example, 'My friend plays with me.'
A house is a building where people live. It usually has rooms like a kitchen, bedroom, and bathroom. For example, 'My family lives in a house.'
A school is a place where children and students learn. Teachers help them study subjects like math, reading, and science. For example, 'I go to school every day.'
Food is what people and animals eat to live. It gives the body energy and strength. For example, 'Rice is my favorite food.'
Water is a clear liquid that people, animals, and plants need to survive. We drink it, cook with it, and use it every day. For example, 'I drink water when I am thirsty.'
A book is a set of pages with writing or pictures. People read books to learn or enjoy stories. For example, 'I read a book before bed.'
Day is the time from morning to evening when the sun is up. It is opposite of night. For example, 'I go to school in the day.'
Night is the time when it is dark outside and people usually sleep. It comes after evening and before morning. For example, 'The stars shine at night.'
Morning is the early part of the day after night. The sun rises in the morning. For example, 'I eat breakfast in the morning.'
Today means the day that is happening right now. It is between yesterday and tomorrow. For example, 'Today is my birthday.'
Tomorrow is the day after today. It has not happened yet. For example, 'Tomorrow we will go to the park.'
The sun is a big star that gives light and heat to Earth. It rises in the morning and sets in the evening. For example, 'The sun is bright today.'
Rain is water that falls from the clouds in the sky. It helps plants grow and fills rivers and lakes. For example, 'It is raining outside.'
Bad means not good, unpleasant, or harmful. For example, 'This food tastes bad.' It is the opposite of good.
Big means large in size or amount. For example, 'The elephant is big.' It is the opposite of small.
Hello is a word people say when they meet or greet someone. It is polite and friendly. For example, 'Hello, how are you?'
My shows that something belongs to the speaker. For example, 'This is my book.' It is a possessive word.
A name is a word we use to call or identify a person, animal, or thing. For example, 'My name is Tom.' Everyone has a name.
Nice means pleasant, kind, or good. For example, 'She is a nice person.' It is often used to describe people or things.
Meet means to see and talk to someone for the first time or again. For example, 'I meet my teacher at school.' Meeting helps people connect.
Your shows that something belongs to the person you are speaking to. For example, 'This is your bag.' It is a possessive word.
Hi is a short and casual way to say hello. People use it with friends or in relaxed situations. For example, 'Hi, how are you?'
How is a word used to ask about the way or condition of something. For example, 'How are you?' means asking about someone’s feeling. It helps start questions.
Fine means good or okay. For example, 'I am fine' means you are doing well. It can also mean good quality, like 'fine clothes.'
Later means after the present time. For example, 'I will call you later.' It shows something will happen afterward.
Goodbye is a word people say when leaving each other. It is the opposite of hello. For example, 'Goodbye, see you tomorrow.'
What is a word used to ask about information. For example, 'What is your name?' It helps find out details or facts.
This means a person or thing that is close to the speaker. For example, 'This is my bag.' It points to something near you.
That means a person or thing farther away from the speaker. For example, 'That is a dog in the yard.' It points to something not near.
A pencil is a tool used for writing or drawing. It usually has wood on the outside and graphite inside. For example, 'I write with a pencil.'
A dog is an animal often kept as a pet or used for work. Dogs are loyal and friendly to people. For example, 'The dog runs in the park.'
Lot means a large amount or number of something. For example, 'I have a lot of homework.' It shows many or much of something.
Many means a large number of people or things. For example, 'Many students are in the classroom.' It is used with countable nouns.
Five is the number 5. For example, 'I have five apples.' It comes after four and before six.
A cat is a small animal kept as a pet. Cats are known for being playful, curious, and sometimes quiet. For example, 'The cat sleeps on the bed.'
Color is what we see when light reflects from things. Examples are red, blue, and green. For example, 'My favorite color is blue.'
Black is a dark color that is the opposite of white. Many objects can be black, like clothes or the night sky. For example, 'He wears a black hat.'

Pizza is a popular food made with dough, tomato sauce, cheese, and often other toppings like vegetables or meat. It is baked in an oven and usually cut into slices to share. People enjoy it at parties, restaurants, or at home because it is easy and tasty.

A hamburger is a sandwich made with a cooked ground beef patty placed inside a bun. It often comes with lettuce, tomato, cheese, and sauces like ketchup or mayonnaise. Many fast-food restaurants serve hamburgers, and they are a common meal around the world.

Favorite means the thing you like the most out of all others. It can describe food, color, sport, or even a person. For example, 'Pizza is my favorite food' means pizza is the food you enjoy the most.

A banana is a long, yellow fruit with soft, sweet flesh inside. It grows in hot countries and is easy to peel and eat. Bananas give you quick energy, so many people eat them as a snack or with breakfast.

A sport is an activity where people play games or compete using physical skill and effort. Examples are soccer, basketball, and tennis. Sports are often played for fun, health, or competition, and they can be team-based or individual.
Kind can mean two things. As a noun, it means a type or category, like 'What kind of food do you like?'. As an adjective, it means being nice or caring toward others, such as 'She is a kind person'.

Basketball is a sport where two teams try to throw a ball through the other team’s hoop. Each team has five players on the court at a time. It is fast, exciting, and played all around the world, both indoors and outdoors.
Sleep is the natural rest your body needs every night. During sleep, you close your eyes and your body recovers energy. Without enough sleep, people feel tired and cannot think or work well.

A couch is a piece of furniture that people sit or lie on, often found in the living room. It usually has cushions and space for several people. Families and friends sit on a couch to watch TV, relax, or talk together.
The is a word used before nouns to talk about something specific. For example, 'the dog' means one particular dog, not any dog. It helps make sentences more clear and exact.
To is a small word used in many ways. It can show direction, like 'go to school', or purpose, like 'I want to learn English to travel'. It often connects verbs and nouns together.
Of is a word that shows a relationship or belonging. For example, 'a cup of water' means water inside a cup. It helps explain parts, amounts, or connections between things.
And is a word used to join two or more ideas together. For example, 'I like apples and bananas' means you like both. It makes sentences longer and connects thoughts smoothly.

A is an article used before a singular noun when talking about one thing, but not a specific one. For example, 'a dog' means any dog, not one you already know. It is often used when first introducing something.
In is a word that shows something is inside a place or time. For example, 'in the box' means inside the box, and 'in the morning' means during that time. It helps explain location or situation.
It is a word used to refer to a thing, animal, or idea already known. For example, 'I have a book. It is blue.' It helps avoid repeating the same noun again and again.
For is a word that shows purpose, reason, or benefit. For example, 'This gift is for you' means the gift is meant to be yours. It also explains time, like 'for two hours'.

On shows that something is above and touching a surface, like 'The book is on the table'. It also talks about time and activities, such as 'on Monday' or 'on TV'. It is a very common preposition in English.
With shows being together or having something. For example, 'I went to the park with my friend' means your friend was there too. It also shows what tool you use, like 'cut with a knife'.
Not is a word that makes a sentence negative. For example, 'I am not hungry' means the opposite of hungry. It is often used with verbs to show something does not happen.
Be is a verb used to talk about existence, identity, or condition. For example, 'I am a student' or 'She is happy'. It changes form into am, is, are, was, or were depending on time and subject.
He is a word used instead of a man or boy’s name. For example, 'This is John. He is my friend.' It is a subject pronoun that helps avoid repeating names.
From shows the starting point of a place, time, or source. For example, 'I am from Korea' means Korea is your origin. It can also show the beginning of time, like 'from morning to night'.
At shows a specific place or time. For example, 'She is at school' means her location is school. It can also describe time, like 'at 7 o’clock'.
Have means to own, hold, or experience something. For example, 'I have a car' means the car belongs to you. It can also mean experiencing, like 'I have lunch' or 'I have a good time'.
Or is a word used to show choice between two or more things. For example, 'Do you want tea or coffee?' It helps ask about options or possibilities.
All means every person or thing in a group. For example, 'all the students' means every student without exception. It can describe people, objects, or even time, like 'all day'.
Will is a word used to talk about the future. For example, 'I will go to school tomorrow' means the action will happen later. It also shows intention or decision.
Like means to enjoy or feel good about something. For example, 'I like music' means music makes you happy. It can also compare things, as in 'She sings like a bird'.
One is the number 1. It can also mean a single person or thing, like 'one apple'. Sometimes it is used to replace a noun, as in 'This is a good one'.

Me is the word you use to talk about yourself when someone else is the subject. It is used after verbs or prepositions, like 'help me' or 'with me.' This word shows that you are the one receiving an action. For example, 'Please give it to me.' Using 'me' makes sentences more personal and direct.

Up means moving to a higher place or position. It can show direction, like going from the ground to the sky. People use 'up' in many expressions, such as 'stand up,' 'wake up,' or 'look up.' It can also describe feelings, like being 'cheered up.' Example: 'She climbed up the hill.'

Can is a word that shows ability or possibility. When you say 'I can swim,' it means you know how to do it. It is also used to ask permission, like 'Can I go outside?' Can is very common in everyday speech. Example: 'He can play the guitar very well.'

No is used to refuse, deny, or disagree with something. It is the opposite of 'yes.' People say 'no' when they don’t want something, or when something is not true. It is also used in polite answers, like 'No, thank you.' Example: 'No, I don’t want to go.'

Out means moving from the inside to the outside. It can describe leaving a house, room, or container. People use it in many phrases, like 'go out,' 'take out,' or 'run out.' It can also mean not available, like 'out of stock.' Example: 'She went out to meet her friends.'

Do means to act, perform, or carry out something. It is used in many questions, like 'Do you like apples?' It also works as a helper verb, such as 'I do not know.' People often say 'do homework' or 'do the dishes.' Example: 'I will do my best.'

There refers to a place that is not here. It can point to something far away or just not close. People also use 'there is' or 'there are' to show that something exists. For example, 'There is a book on the table.' It helps make sentences clear and complete.

A girl is a female child or young woman. Girls can be daughters, sisters, or friends. They go to school, play, and learn just like boys. The word 'girl' is often used to talk about age before someone becomes a woman. Example: 'The girl is reading a storybook.'

After means later in time or following something. If you eat lunch after school, lunch comes second. It can also mean behind in order, like 'B comes after A.' People use it in both time and place. Example: 'We went for ice cream after dinner.'

New means something that has just been made, bought, or discovered. It is the opposite of old. People use it to describe clothes, ideas, or experiences. New things often feel fresh and exciting. Example: 'She bought a new phone yesterday.'

Get means to receive, obtain, or become something. You can get a gift, get tired, or get better at a skill. It is a very flexible word in English. People use it in many daily situations, like 'get home' or 'get ready.' Example: 'I will get a letter tomorrow.'
A man is an adult male person. The word is used when a boy grows up. Men can be fathers, brothers, workers, or leaders. It is the opposite of 'woman.' Example: 'The man is fixing his car.'

Time is what we measure with seconds, minutes, and hours. It tells us when things happen and how long they last. People talk about time with clocks, calendars, and seasons. Time can pass quickly or slowly depending on what you do. Example: 'I don’t have much time today.'

Last means coming at the end or most recent. It can describe the final thing in a list or event. People say 'last week' or 'last night' to talk about something that already happened. It can also mean continue, as in 'The show will last two hours.' Example: 'This is the last piece of cake.'

Good means nice, right, or of high quality. It describes people, food, or experiences that make us happy. The opposite of good is bad. People often say 'good morning,' 'good job,' or 'good idea.' Example: 'She is a good friend.'

Now means the present time. It shows what is happening at this very moment. People use 'now' to talk about something urgent or immediate. Example: 'Please come here now.' It makes the action feel current and important.

Any means one or some, no matter which. It is often used in questions or negatives, like 'Do you have any money?' or 'I don’t have any friends here.' It shows no limit to choice. Example: 'You can take any book you like.'

Down means moving to a lower place or level. It can describe direction, like going down stairs. People use it to mean sadness, as in 'feeling down.' Example: 'He sat down on the chair.' It is often the opposite of up.
Go means to move from one place to another. People go to school, go home, or go outside. It is a very common verb for movement. Example: 'Let’s go to the park.' It shows action and travel.

First means before all others in order or time. It shows the beginning of something. People say 'first place' in a race or 'first day' at school. Example: 'She was the first to arrive.' It is the opposite of last.

Work means activity done to earn money or achieve something. People go to work every day in offices, schools, or shops. It can also mean effort, like 'This plan will work.' Example: 'He is busy with his work.' Work is an important part of life.

Open means not closed or shut. Doors, windows, and boxes can be open. It also means ready to accept ideas, like 'open to suggestions.' Example: 'The store is open from 9 to 5.' It gives the idea of freedom and access.
Very means to a high degree. It makes words stronger, like 'very big' or 'very happy.' People use it to show strong feelings. Example: 'She is very smart.' It helps make language more expressive.

Think means to use your mind to form ideas or solve problems. People think about the past, future, or choices they must make. It can also mean having an opinion. Example: 'I think this book is interesting.' Thinking is part of learning.

A window is an opening in a wall with glass that lets in light and air. People look through windows to see outside. Windows can open or close for fresh air. Example: 'She opened the window to let in the breeze.' They are found in most buildings and homes.

Right can mean correct, like giving the right answer. It can also mean the opposite of left in direction. People use 'right now' to show immediacy. Example: 'Turn right at the corner.' Right is often about correctness or direction.

Back means the rear part of something, like the back of a chair. It can also mean returning to a place, like 'go back home.' People use it to talk about support, as in 'I’ve got your back.' Example: 'She looked back and waved.'

People are men, women, and children together. The word means more than one person. People live in towns, cities, and countries. They work, play, and share culture. Example: 'Many people came to the party.'
Too means also, or in addition. It can also mean more than needed, like 'too hot' or 'too big.' Example: 'I like pizza too.' People use it in both positive and negative ways.
See means to notice something with your eyes. People see colors, people, and places. It can also mean understand, as in 'I see your point.' Example: 'I can see the stars tonight.'
Off means away from or not working. Lights can be off, or someone can take off shoes. It shows separation from something. Example: 'The TV is off.' It is often the opposite of on.
Make means to create or produce something. People make food, art, or plans. It also means causing something to happen, like 'make me happy.' Example: 'She will make a cake for the party.'
Want means to wish to have or do something. People want food, toys, or time to rest. It shows desire or need. Example: 'I want to go outside.' It is common in everyday speech.
Here means in this place. It shows that something is close to the speaker. Example: 'Come here, please.' People use it to point to a location or presence.
Before means earlier than something in time. Breakfast comes before lunch. It can also mean in front of in space. Example: 'She stood before the class.' It shows both time and position.
Really means truly or in fact. It makes words stronger, like 'really good' or 'really fast.' People use it to show honesty or surprise. Example: 'Do you really mean it?'

Say means to speak words. People say hello, thank you, or important ideas. It can also mean repeat what someone else said. Example: 'She says she is tired.' It is one of the most common verbs in English.
Day is the time from morning until night. It also means a full 24 hours. People talk about special days, like birthdays or holidays. Example: 'It was a sunny day.' Days mark the passing of time.
A boy is a male child. Boys can be sons, brothers, or classmates. They grow up to become men. Example: 'The boy is playing football.' The word is the opposite of girl.

Long describes something that measures much from end to end. It can also mean lasting a lot of time. People say 'a long road' or 'a long day.' Example: 'The movie was very long.' It is the opposite of short.
